name: Linagliptin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Linagliptin, a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor, is mostly cleared outside the kidneys (renal excretion under 5%). The US label recommends no dose adjustment at any level of kidney function.
kidney_function_basis: Label states no adjustment for renal impairment.

bands.recommendation: 5 mg once daily; no adjustment (label). Studied in CARMELINA (15% had eGFR <30).
No adjustment recommended for renal impairment (label).

hd.text: No adjustment in label; removal by hemodialysis is unlikely (label).

pd.text: No adjustment in label; removal by peritoneal dialysis is unlikely (label).

monitoring: Hypoglycemia with sulfonylureas or insulin; pancreatitis; bullous pemphigoid.

pediatric.approved_ages: Safety and effectiveness not established; a 26-week pediatric trial (10–17 years) did not show effectiveness (label).
pediatric.egfr_equation: Bedside Schwartz: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) = 0.413 x height (cm) / serum creatinine (mg/dL)

sources.citation: Boehringer Ingelheim Pharmaceuticals, Inc.. (2025). Tradjenta (linagliptin) [Prescribing information; US FDA-approved label, NDA201280, set ID c797ea5c-cab7-494b-9044-27eba0cfe40f, version effective March 21, 2025]. DailyMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine.

adult: Label's 'no adjustment' covers renal impairment generally; dialysis patients are not explicitly addressed beyond 'removal unlikely'.
